University of Toronto Rocketry Design Team
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

### INTRODUCTION

::: {.two-col-side}

::: {}
![](utat_tank/images/problem.jpg)
:::

::: {}
- Analyzed and optimized the bulkheads and fuel tanks of UTAT's liquid propellent rocket
- Existing design was thought to be underengineered by team leads and susceptible to bearing failure at expected operating pressures based on an inaccessible prior FEA
- Performed detailed structural analysis with FEA and hand calculations, updated bulkheads to meet fluid volume requirements, selected O-rings,and produced engineering drawings
:::

:::

### PROCESS

::: {.two-col-cards}

::: {.step-card}
- Researched bolted joint analysis and performed hand calculations to determine stresses for each failure mode, including bolt tear out, casing tensile failure, bolt shear failure, and bearing failure
:::

::: {.step-card}
-  Contrary to prior belief, my calculations showed that the tank was overengineered with a safety factor of 3, and that bolt shear was the actual governing failure mode
:::

:::

::: {.two-col-cards}

::: {.step-card}
![](utat_tank/images/broken_bulkhead.png)

- Validated analysis via hydrostatic burst testing; tank withstood >2.5x design pressure and failed via bolt shear, exactly as predicted
:::

::: {.step-card}
![](utat_tank/images/broken_bolts.png)

- Built design sheet with Excel to automate calculations and determine optimal tank geometry for reduced weight
:::

:::

::: {.two-col-cards}

::: {.step-card}
![](utat_tank/images/bulkhead_cad.png)

- Reduced factor of safety to 1.75 by decreasing tank wall thickness by 33% and bolt count by 20%
- Implemented shoulder bolts to improve tank resistance to bolt shear failure
- Redesigned bulkheads with Onshape for updated fluid volumes and produced engineering drawings
:::

::: {.step-card}
![](utat_tank/images/drawing.png)

- Selected temperature- and chemical-compatible O-rings
- Implemented groove dimensions and tolerances to match Parker handbook recommendations for proper sealing
:::

:::

::: {.two-image-row}

::: {}
![](utat_tank/images/bulkhead_fea.png)
:::

::: {}
![](utat_tank/images/downcomer_fea.png)
:::

:::

- Conducted FEA with ANSYS on final bulkheads and downcomer tube
- Calculated worst-case thermal deformation of propellent tank walls to resolve Launch Canada's concern that the downcomer (tube carrying fuel through the oxider tank) would fail due to thermal contraction, showing a safety factor in excess of 3.5

### RESULTS

::: {.two-image-row}

::: {}
![](utat_tank/images/cad.png)
:::

::: {}
![](utat_tank/images/manufacturing.jpg)
:::

:::

- Fuel tank wall thickness reduced by 33% and bolt count by 20%
- Maintained a safety factor >1.5 on all components for a 1000 psi maximum expected operating pressure
- Addressed Launch Canada's concerns regarding the downcomer, allowing retention of existing design

:::
